strand_a.title: Autonomy through partnerships: Charting the EU's global digital engagement
strand_a.summary: As geopolitical competition intensifies, the EU needs a more coherent external digital strategy that complements its pursuit of digital sovereignty. Drawing on 199 EU-led digital initiatives across all major regions and five domains, the Analysis shows that the Union's global engagement extends beyond regulation to infrastructure, research, cybersecurity and security cooperation. Armenia's association to Horizon Europe illustrates growing partner demand for access to EU programmes and innovation ecosystems. The report argues for selective long-term partnerships that expand European capabilities, reduce strategic dependencies and anchor the EU more deeply in global digital value chains.

strand_a.title: Back to the future? What it will take to deliver nuclear energy in the EU – CEPS
strand_a.summary: The growing role of non-EU technology vendors for large-scale reactors and SMRs on the EU market raises questions about technological sovereignty, industrial competitiveness and strategic dependencies. The report also discusses the long-term political commitment, regulatory predictability and financing frameworks required to de-risk highly capital-intensive investment.

strand_a.title: Prospects for EU–Asia donor partnerships in international development – CEPS
strand_a.summary: The report examines EU–Asia donor partnerships as the United States retreats from traditional ODA and China consolidates an infrastructure-led alternative. It frames the EU's Global Gateway as investment-led geopolitical statecraft, with digital transformation, energy, transport, health and education investment presented as part of a values-based alternative in a competitive geopolitical environment.

strand_b.title: Co-creating climate-resilient cities: a multi-method participatory approach for future scenario building and prioritization
strand_b.authors: Havva Ebrahimipour, Monika Mačiulienė, Anna Maria Kotrikla, Franz-Ferdinand Rothe, Gintarė Gulevičiūtė, Aelita Skaržauskienė, Kristina Kovaitė, Amalia Polydoropoulou, et al.
strand_b.summary: The study introduces and tests a multi-method participatory foresight framework for developing locally grounded climate-resilient urban futures, aiming to bridge community-led visioning and formal administrative prioritization. It contributes a replicable future-oriented planning methodology relevant to policy and innovation practice.

strand_b.title: Governance logics and foresight functions: European strategic foresight in contrastive perspective
strand_b.summary: The article develops a governance-sensitive framework that links foresight methods to institutional functions in public decision-making. It compares how identical foresight methods perform different functions across technocratic, market-managerial, networked and anticipatory governance settings.

strand_b.title: Circular futures under institutional diversity: which organisations and circular practice forms thrive, where and why
strand_b.authors: Brais Suárez-Eiroa, Tommaso Calzolari, Aitor Alonso-Rodríguez
